messages:
jamie: Heads up — hitting a flaky case in our streaming SDK. If an auth token rotates mid-SSE stream the server sometimes returns a short 'retry' event and then a 401. Clients tear down, and we occasionally surface partial JSON objects (truncated) to the app which crashes. Anyone have a resilient client pattern for: reconnection + resume + avoiding partial JSON emission?
cheng: Seen that before. Two main pieces: 1) server emits stable event IDs (and ideally an offset) so client can reconnect with Last-Event-ID and resume; 2) client must buffer/reassemble partial frames and only emit completed JSON objects. If resume is impossible, server should emit a checkpoint event prior to auth boundary.
sam: On the SDK side we should do all of that automatically. Short plan: incremental JSON reassembler + single automatic token refresh + reconnect with Last-Event-ID header. If we still get 401 after refresh, surface a clear error. Avoid emitting parse errors to app: keep partial buffer until we can confirm it's complete.
taylor: For backpressure, server should honor small write windows. Clients should expose pause/resume on their stream. Node: stream.pause() / stream.resume(). Browser fetch streams: use ReadableStream controller.desiredSize to implement backpressure. Also set a maxQueuedBytes limit on the client and drop/reconnect if exceeded.
marta: Server-side tips: send regular heartbeats (e.g., ":\n\n" or a ping event) so client doesn't assume a mid-stream 401 is just a long delay. Also include event id and an "offset" field when practical.
replay-bot: Logged incident for trace: incident_id=evt-20260317-8491, correlator=jamie, logs at s3://redwood-logs/sse/2026/03/17/evt-8491.log :thumbsup:
sam: Node incremental parse example (very rough):
```js
const clarinet = require('clarinet');
const parser = clarinet.createStream();
let buffer = '';
parser.on('value', v => { buffer += v }); // simplified; use a real incremental library
parser.on('end', () => { try { const obj = JSON.parse(buffer); emit(obj); buffer = ''; } catch(e) { /* wait for more chunks */ } });
fetch(url, { headers }).then(res => { res.body.on('data', chunk => parser.write(chunk)); });
```
sam: For Node we recommend using a tested incremental json parser (clarinet/oboe/JSONStream) instead of ad-hoc concatenation. For Python, use ijson or yajl with response.content.iter_chunked and feed the parser.
cheng: Resume header example (server): add event id per SSE `id: evt-12345` and client reconnects: `GET /stream` with `Last-Event-ID: evt-12345` so server can send events after that id. If server can't resume mid-transaction, send a checkpoint event `event: checkpoint\ndata: {"offset": 12345}` before the auth boundary.
jamie: How do we handle duplicates on resume? If server re-sends the last event or two for safety we'll dedupe on the client based on id?
taylor: Yes — client-side dedupe using recent event-id cache (sliding window) is simplest. Keep a small ring buffer of recent IDs or record highest offset seen per stream. If events are idempotent, that's even easier.
marta: Also think about partial JSON that spans reconnect: if you can't resume in the middle of a JSON object, the server should be responsible for ensuring objects are re-emitted whole after resume, or emit smaller chunked messages that reconstruct deterministically.
sam: SDK actionables: implement incremental reassembler + Last-Event-ID reconnect + one-shot token refresh + dedupe by event id. Will add config flags: maxBufferBytes, maxRetryAttempts, enableIdDedup.
jamie: That sounds great. can we get a small repro harness to run against the runtime where we force a 401 mid-stream? I can file a test and attach to the incident.
cheng: I'll add a server-side test that emits an id, then half an object, then returns 401. If last-event-id provided, server will resume after that id.
marta: I'll draft a short doc with recommended server behavior (emit ids, keep checkpoints, heartbeats) and client SDK recommendations.
sam: I'll open a PR for the SDK reassembler with a minimal node + python example. ping me if you want early review.
jamie: Thanks all — assigning follow-ups: sam -> SDK PR, cheng -> server resume test, marta -> doc. Will update incident when repro is linked. :thumbsup:
